label: Video generation & motion
note: Everything that turns a still into moving pictures, plus the control recipes layered on top and the candidates that were refused for licence or hardware reasons.

entities.name: AnimateDiff
entities.summary: 1xxx-roster motion for SD1.5-era stills. Gone by the time the 2xxx roster was written; no measured comparison survives.

entities.name: Stable Video Diffusion
entities.summary: In the pre-July roster as the I2V option; replaced by Wan2.1 before any dated bench on this box.

entities.name: Deforum
entities.summary: Camera/keyframe animation from the SD1.5 era, replaced by control-frame recipes on a real video model.

entities.name: Wan2.1-I2V-14B
entities.where: comfy workflows wan22_i2v.json / VACE graphs on :8188
entities.summary: The engine that carried every clip for five months, always through the VACE control recipe. Apache-2.0 throughout, which is why all 41 captured video graphs passed the licence gate.

issues.text: Plain I2V ignored prompted motion — the shift parameter turned out to be the lever, not the prompt.
609 s for a 5 s clip at 832x480, and 2074.8 s (34.6 min) for 5 s at 960² with 20 steps cfg 5 — the reason the lane was replaced.
480p only on the VACE recipe.
Still keeps finer skin and freckle texture than its replacement, measured side by side on the same still and seed. The texture gap is a real regression the new engine has not closed.
No audio.

entities.name: VACE control-frame recipe
entities.summary: The recipe that made Wan usable: control frames carrying identity from PIXELS, with strength for motion and modality for identity. Chunked on 09-20 into 5 x 25 frames with a 7-frame overlap cross-fade at strength 0.8.

issues.text: Single-pass VACE could not hold a long clip; the chained-chunk recipe (5 x 25 frames, 7-frame overlap, strength 0.8) was accepted at take 10 of 8 full takes.
VACE can paint the CONTROL PLATE itself — a flat grey humanoid with the OpenPose limb bars visible — instead of the character. Same failure family as the 09-15 blob/fire fixture.
97 frames cost 999 s at 29.3 GB peak.

entities.name: Wan2.2-I2V-A14B
entities.summary: Installed and validated on 2026-08-09 but never cut over: the production switch waits on a motion gate and an identity A/B that were never run. Character LoRAs fit the LOW expert only.

issues.text: Production cutover held pending a motion-gate and identity A/B — still not run, so the lane skipped past it to LTX-2.5.
Character LoRAs fit the LOW expert only in the dual-expert split.

entities.name: Wan Lightning 4-step
entities.summary: 4x faster than full Wan sampling and left off on purpose: it buys speed by trading away the motion that was prompted.

issues.text: Swaps prompted motion for a camera pan — the subject stops doing what the prompt asked. Same motion drop later seen on an LTX tractor clip.

entities.name: Wan-Animate
entities.summary: Tried as a full-body-reference replacement for VACE and refused on the first real take.

issues.text: Rendered a frozen grey statue and ignored the pose entirely.

entities.name: LTX-2.5 22B distilled
entities.summary: 5 s at 960² with stereo audio in 25 s wall against Wan's 609 s, identity held, on its own ComfyUI instance sharing the production weights library. The only open-weights candidate that is both legal here and runnable on one 4090.

issues.text: 24x faster than the engine it replaced: 25.4 s wall for 5 s 960² 24 fps with AAC stereo, against 609 s (and 2074.8 s at matched settings) for Wan 2.2.
Brought audio into the same pass — Wan had none.

Goes soft/smoothed in mid-clip profile frames where Wan kept skin and freckle texture. Not closed by the dev checkpoint: dev + distilled LoRA looks like distilled, and dev full with a hand-rolled 15-step schedule came out SOFTER (freckles lost mid-clip).
30 s / 721 frames at 960² is the hard ceiling on the 4090 (peak 48217 of 49140 MiB); 33 s will not fit.

A free-running 30 s render DRIFTS BADLY — by 15 s a snake mane dissolved into ordinary human hair and never came back. 10 s holds. Fixed by pinning the last frame (LTXVAddGuide frame_idx=-1, strength 0.7 = 0 frozen frames, best seam), not by a better prompt.
The painted/Arcane look drifts toward smooth photoreal mid-clip and the face wanders — the distilled model leans photoreal. A style LoRA is the predicted fix; not built.

It invents camera moves and framing unless the prompt forbids them: an early take pulled the camera back and invented a window. The fix is direction, not a seed — 'Locked-off static camera, no camera movement, no zoom, the framing never changes' held all three later takes.
Any reach-away action turns the face to profile and can lose it (a 'dips the quill' take went profile for ~2 s; a character told to turn his head turned his back instead).
No identity bench for Abel or Cornelis, no 9:16 run, and IC-LoRA union control (depth/pose/canny) is not installed.
Loop clips ship silent — a 30 s audio track does not loop.

entities.name: LTX-2.5 22B dev (full)
entities.role: quality checkpoint for the same engine
entities.summary: The undistilled 21.5 GB checkpoint, installed and measured against the distilled default on the same seed. It did not win, so the default stayed distilled.

issues.text: dev + distilled-LoRA-450 at 8 steps = 40 s and looks like distilled; dev full at 15 steps with the official guider values = 50 s and came out SOFTER. The official Full workflow needs RES4LYF ClownSampler + MultimodalGuider, which is not installed.

entities.name: LTX-2.5 A2V (audio-to-video)
entities.role: lip-synced clips from a narration wav
entities.summary: The audio-driven mode that renders a talking character against a narration track. It drove all 138 clips of the portfolio film.

issues.text: Floors clip length to 8-frame blocks, which cut the tail off a line. Fixed by padding the wav rather than by changing the render.

It invents PROPS from the action text — 'points to the list' produced a parchment. The cure is to rewrite the action ('nothing in his paws'), not to re-seed: rewritten actions killed every invented prop, but 15 clips still carry props read out of their action text.

entities.name: LTX-2.5 IC-LoRA pack (14 official)
entities.summary: All 14 official 2.5 IC-LoRAs plus the three 2.3 control adapters the official workflows load, in the shared library and not yet wired into any pipeline.

issues.text: Installed but unused: the refine-details pass is the next untried lever for the texture gap against Wan, and union/motion-track control is not installed at all.
§3.5 of the licence says LoRAs cannot be transferred to a commercial entity.

entities.name: MiniMax H3
entities.summary: Refused on licence: the terms exclude the EU — outputs may not be used outside the licensed territory.

issues.text: EU exclusion. No measurement was attempted; the licence ends it.

entities.name: MAGI-2
entities.summary: Refused on hardware: it needs 8 Hopper GPUs and 307 GB. Nothing wrong with it that this box can fix.

issues.text: Requires 8 Hopper GPUs + 307 GB — unrunnable on one 4090.

entities.name: Wan 2.5 / 2.6 / 2.7 / 3.0
entities.summary: The later Wan generations are API-only, not open weights — a first read wrongly called 2.7 open, corrected the same day.

issues.text: API-only: no weights to run locally, so the whole lane's local-first rule rules them out.

entities.name: HunyuanVideo
entities.summary: Same Tencent EU exclusion that removed the image→mesh family. Refused without a bench.

issues.text: Tencent EU exclusion.

entities.name: Seedance 2.x (CapCut)
entities.role: the quality bar that triggered the migration
entities.summary: The hosted model whose 10 s photoreal clip embarrassed the local stack into the LTX migration. Closed weights, served on a fleet, 10x distilled with RLHF over three reward models and cherry-picked demos.

issues.text: Closed: cannot be run or licensed here. Kept in the record as the reference point for what a fleet-served distilled model looks like.
